key_insight: Language models can act as Research World Models that predict which experimental interventions will work, and their predictions improve when they are given prior research experience.
engineering_relevance: This helps AI research agents choose higher-value experiments under tight compute budgets, reducing wasted trial-and-error in model development workflows.
method: Evaluate LMs as outcome predictors for candidate interventions across 9 research environments.
Inject research experience from real experiments, both within the same environment and across environments.
Compare ranking quality and downstream selection regret under fixed experimental budgets.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes over 2,600 experimental records across pretraining, post-training, and inference, representing more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on available experimental history, so transfer may be weaker in novel environments with little or no prior data.
paper_title: Language Models as AI Research World Models
